In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the maturation of the kidney is a dynamic process that continues throughout the lifespan of the organism and that K+ transport mechanisms in the maturing distal nephron are subject to regulation by a variety of hormonal, metabolic, and developmental factors.
K+ transport is a complex process involving multiple transporters and channels, the expression and activity of which are regulated at multiple levels.
the regulation of K+ balance is complex and involves a variety of factors that may be influenced by a variety of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maturing kidney has the capacity to regulate K+ balance and that this regulation is mediated primarily by the distal nephrons.
the maturing kidney undergoes a developmental switch in K+ handling.
the maturing kidney has the ability to adapt K+ transport to the needs of the organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maturing distal nephron is a major site for the regulation of K+ balance.

the K+ transport machinery in the maturing and adult kidney is similar, but the relative contribution of each component differs, and that this is due to the presence of a unique K+ transporter (the H-K-ATPase) and the absence of a unique K+-secretory channel (the secretory K+ channel).
the distal nephrons and colon are not only the major sites of K+ transport, but also the major targets for regulation of K+ homeostasis.
